flows.narrative: Unchanged and re-confirmed this run: still only the week-ended-18-Nov figures (global equity funds +$59.23bn Lipper / +$66.6bn BofA, 9th straight week; US equities +$45.71bn, largest since 23 Sep; tech funds +$12.3bn Lipper). New detail found this run: the Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.1 from 7.4 (driven by EM-debt and high-yield outflows and wider credit spreads); EM debt saw -$7.5bn outflows (most since April 2020) even as EM equities kept drawing +$1.98-8.3bn inflows -- a debt/equity divergence; Europe gained +$1.5bn (most since Feb) while Japan lost -$4.2bn (biggest since May). This window (through Wed 18 Nov) still predates the Nov 20 crash, Nov 23 Nvidia-driven rebound, and Nov 24 pullback entirely -- the week-ending-25-Nov edition will be the first to show any reaction. Separately, prime-brokerage data (Goldman, via Tickmill) shows hedge funds stayed net sellers of US equities for a 3rd straight week into Monday's rally and single-stock short volume hit its largest weekly pace since June 2022 -- Monday's +4.73% S&P bounce was short-covering (hedge funds forced to cover a ~$19bn short book after selling ~$57bn over the prior month, Goldman desk conviction only 5/10), not fresh institutional buying; retail (Vanda) kept buying dips, net +$3.49bn into Nvidia alone from Nov 4-23.
